skills.name: Precise Action Parameter Construction
skills.description: When the agent correctly identifies what action to take but constructs the API call with wrong arguments — such as incorrect item IDs, wrong payment method, wrong flight numbers, wrong amounts, or wrong cancellation reasons — the task fails despite correct strategic intent. The agent must translate user preferences into exact, system-valid parameter values by carefully cross-referencing all retrieved data.
skills.reasoning: Both domains show the agent choosing the right function but supplying wrong parameter values — wrong flight numbers, wrong item IDs, wrong amounts, wrong reason codes — indicating a consistent gap between strategic intent and precise execution.

skills.name: Business Rule and Policy Compliance
skills.description: The agent takes technically executable actions that violate domain policy — such as modifying or cancelling non-changeable tickets, issuing unsolicited compensation beyond policy limits, or applying refunds to ineligible transaction types. The agent must check whether an action is permitted under policy before executing it, even when the underlying API does not enforce the constraint.
skills.reasoning: In both domains, the agent executes API calls that succeed technically but produce a wrong database state because they bypass business rules — cancelling non-refundable reservations, modifying locked items, over-compensating customers — revealing the agent does not enforce policy constraints before acting.

skills.name: Multi-Step Plan Completion
skills.description: In tasks requiring a sequence of sub-actions, the agent completes only part of the workflow — stopping after the first sub-task, forgetting a required downstream step, or failing to cascade a first action into its necessary follow-up. The agent must hold the full task plan in working memory and verify each step is done before closing the interaction.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains, multi-step requests (cancel-then-rebook, modify-then-update-bag, return-and-also-cancel) regularly see the agent complete only the first step and stop, demonstrating a deficit in maintaining and executing a full sequential plan.

skills.name: Identity and Reference Resolution
skills.description: The agent fails to correctly identify the user account or the specific item, order, or reservation being discussed — either because authentication lookup fails due to wrong credentials, the agent does not extract all identifying information from conversational context, or it selects the wrong entity among several candidates. The agent must persistently probe for correct identifiers and infer implicit references from conversation history.
skills.reasoning: Both domains show failures where the agent either cannot look up the user (wrong email, wrong zip, missing last name), selects the wrong reservation out of multiple candidates, or stops working after the first failed lookup rather than trying alternative identifiers.

skills.name: Accurate Numerical Reporting
skills.description: The agent fails to compute or communicate specific numerical values — totals, price differences, refund amounts, item counts, or transaction identifiers — with the precision required by the task. The agent must perform and verify calculations, then explicitly state the precise figures expected by the user rather than rounding, estimating, or omitting them.
skills.reasoning: In both domains, tasks require the agent to either calculate amounts correctly and communicate them explicitly; failures include wrong totals, missing price differences, omitted tracking numbers, and uncommunicated savings — a cross-domain pattern of numerical imprecision.

skills.name: Task Focus Under Social Pressure
skills.description: When users apply flattery, emotional distress, repeated manipulation, or extended social digressions, the agent loses focus on task completion — either abandoning the task goal to reciprocate socially, over-compensating due to emotional pressure, or failing to redirect the conversation back to the pending action. The agent must maintain professional task orientation regardless of the emotional register of the conversation.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains, users who are excessively flattering, grieving, or conversationally chaotic cause the agent to abandon its task goal — either entering an endless social exchange loop, adding unauthorized goodwill gestures, or spending all turns on tangential exchanges instead of completing the requested action.
